etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French dose, from Late Latin dosis, from Ancient Greek δόσις (dósis, “a portion prescribed”, literally “a giving”), used by Galen and other Greek physicians to mean an amount of medicine, from δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to give”). Doublet of doos.

definitions.definition: A measured portion of medicine taken at any one time.
The quantity of an agent (not always active) substance or radiation administered or experienced at any one time.

quote.citation: 2014 April 21, “Subtle effects”, in The Economist, volume 411, number 8884:
quote.text: Manganism has been known about since the 19th century, when miners exposed to ores containing manganese […] began to totter, slur their speech and behave like someone inebriated. The poisoning was irreversible, and soon ended in psychosis and death. Nowadays workers are exposed to far lower doses and manganism is rare.

definitions.definition: (figurative, dated) Anything disagreeable that must be taken.
(figurative, dated) A good measure or lengthy experience of something.

quote.citation: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I, page 197:
quote.text: “I had then, as you remember, just returned to London after a lot of Indian Ocean, Pacific, China Seas - a regular dose of the East - six years or so, and I was loafing about, hindering you fellows in your work and invading your homes, just as though I had got a heavenly mission to civilise you.”
The prospect of becoming a father is a dose of reality that threatens to bring his dream world crashing down.

quote.citation: 1972, Shel Silverstein (lyrics and music), “Don't Give A Dose to the One You Love Most”:
quote.text: Don't give a dose to the one you love most. / Give her some marmalade... give her some toast.

quote.citation: 1978, Lawrence Durrell, Livia (Avignon Quintet), Faber & Faber, published 1992, page 382:
quote.text: It would be very expensive to cure a dose here, as well as unbelievably painful.

definitions.definition: (Ireland, colloquial) A cold; a common, viral illness of the nasal passage, sometimes with fever.

quote.citation: 1977, The White Buffalo, Wild Bill Hickok:
quote.text: Sometime back, one of your scarlet sisters dosed me proper.

quote.citation: 1839, Benjamin Abbott, Experience and Gospel Labors of the Rev. Benjamin Abbott:
quote.text: Just at the dawning of the day, I fell into a dose more like sleep than any I had during the whole night, in which I dreamed that I saw a river as clear as crystal  […]

quote.citation: 1918, William Henry Hudson, Far Away And Long Ago:
quote.text: It was to me a marvellous experience; to be here, propped up with pillows in a dimly-lighted room, the night-nurse idly dosing by the fire; the sound of the everlasting wind in my ears, howling outside  […]
